subject: Dedicated capacity timeline, OEM lead times & cloud reserve for ACME deal
messages:
From: Liam Holt <liam.holt@acmecorp.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Chris O'Neill <chris.oneill@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-02-12T09:15:00-05:00
Subject: Timeline and lead times for dedicated capacity (ACME)

Rafael —

Thanks for the quick run-through on Friday. Procurement needs an estimate for hardware/vendor lead times to finalize our internal SOW and PO schedule. High-level asks:

- Can Redwood confirm realistic lead times to have dedicated GPU capacity in prod (us-east) if we commit to the deal next week?
- What are the options between reserved cloud instances (AVACLoud) vs. Redwood-managed OEM pods (NVIDIA OEM hardware)?
- Do you have formal OEM quotes we can attach to our procurement package?

We are aiming for a go-live window in late May. If that timeline is infeasible, please flag and suggest mitigations.

Thanks,
Liam Holt
Procurement Manager, ACME Corp

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-02-12T11:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Timeline and lead times for dedicated capacity (ACME)

Liam / Chris —

Appreciate the note. Short answer: we can hit a late-May target with a mix of reserved cloud capacity + staggered OEM shipments, but there are tradeoffs and some near-term contingencies we should accept in the SOW.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) Internal sizing confirmation (attached: redwood_prelim_sizing.xlsx) — Vivek, can you validate the 60-node starting point and call out any SKU constraints?
2) Request formal OEM quote and lead-time commit from NVIDIA (Priya, I will loop you in on this thread).
3) AvaCloud (Jake) — please confirm region-level reserved capacity timelines and whether a firm allocation can be held for an April PO and May activation.
4) We'll produce a short procurement packet for ACME that includes both a reserved-cloud path (faster activation, slightly higher variable cost) and OEM pod path (capex + longer lead).

I'll start reaching out to OEM and cloud ops now. Expect a technical note from Vivek within 24h and an OEM quote request in the next message.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_prelim_sizing.xlsx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Liam Holt <liam.holt@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Jake Robertson <jake.robertson@avacloud.com>
Date: 2026-02-13T08:20:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Timeline and lead times for dedicated capacity (ACME)

Folks —

Quick technical read on the sizing spreadsheet Rafael attached. I ran a short simulation against ACME's target (200 qps peak, 2.5s p95 SLO) using our model footprint assumptions. Notes below and attached a short PDF: fleet_sizing_notes.pdf.

Key takeaways:
- 60 x H100 80GB-class GPUs (or equivalents) looks to be the most straightforward path for latency and single-request concurrency.
- OEM lead time estimate (NVIDIA OEM channel): 10–14 weeks for H100-class racks from PO to full delivery; A100 availability still variable but could be 6–10 weeks if we accept mixed SKUs.
- Cloud reserved capacity (AvaCloud / major cloud): reservation + validation typically 2–6 weeks depending on region and current utilization; firm capacity guarantees require signed commitment and an early reservation deposit (cloud vendor dependent).
- Short-term alternatives: staged capacity (reserve 20–30% in cloud initially, supplement with OEM pods later), pre-emptible/spot fallback for non-critical workloads, and model quantization to reduce node count by ~20% in some cases.

Operational ask for ACME team: please confirm the model(s) you intend to serve (model name + token-length profile) and the target SLOs per route. That will materially change node counts.

Attachment: fleet_sizing_notes.pdf

-Vivek
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
From: Chris O'Neill <chris.oneill@acmecorp.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam Holt <liam.holt@acmecorp.com>, Jake Robertson <jake.robertson@avacloud.com>
Date: 2026-02-14T10:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Timeline and lead times for dedicated capacity (ACME)

Thanks — that helps. A few clarifications from our side:

- ACME target: 200 qps peak across two primary routes (chat + summarize), p95 latency target 2.5s, typical prompt length ~120 tokens, long tail up to 1024 tokens for summarize.
- Preference: we'd like to lean toward Redwood-managed OEM pods for predictable perf, but procurement will need a firm quote and delivery window.
- Pricing: can you provide an estimated cost delta (per month) between a fully OEM-based deployment vs. a hybrid cloud-reserved + OEM fallback approach?

Jake — if AvaCloud can provide a firm reservation schedule (dates + deposit terms) that would be helpful for our procurement packet.

We'll get the formal PO team started once we have the OEM quote and an internal CAPEX timeline.

-Chris
Director, Product Ops — ACME Corp

Subject: Request for formal OEM quote & AvaCloud reservation confirmation — ACME DEAL-2026-0347

Priya / Jake —

Looping you both in per ACME's ask (details below). Attached is a short requirement brief for ACME's anticipated footprint and performance constraints (ACME_requirement_brief.pdf). High level ask:

- Priya: can NVIDIA OEM provide a formal quote for 60x H100 80GB-class nodes (or nearest equivalent) including estimated lead time, partial-shipment options, payment terms, and warranty/onsite options? Please include any volume discounts and typical deposit requirements.
- Jake: can AvaCloud confirm whether us-east-1 has 60-node reservation capacity by May 15 with a deposit/commit? If not, what is the fastest reservation path and dates? Also list any blackout or maintenance windows that could impact provisioning.

We have a target internal approval window by 02/26 to finalize SOW/DocuSign. Rafael will consolidate and attach the OEM quote to the procurement packet. HubSpot link: https://hub.redwood.ai/deals/DEAL-2026-0347

Attachment: ACME_requirement_brief.pdf

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@nvidia-oem.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya.SalesOps <sales.ops@nvidia-oem.com>
Date: 2026-02-16T16:40:00-05:00
Subject: NVIDIA OEM quote & lead time — initial response

Rafael / Marissa —

Thanks for the details and the brief. Preliminary response below — formal quote attached as PDF (NVIDIA_QUOTE_20260216.pdf).

Summary:
- SKU: H100 80GB-class (full fat) recommended for ACME's latency profile.
- Quantity: 60 nodes (we can propose a staged shipment: 20 units in ~8 weeks, remaining in 10–14 weeks depending on fab allocations).
- Lead time: we estimate 10–14 weeks from PO for the full order. Partial shipments possible (first tranche ~8 weeks).
- Terms: OEM channel typically requires 30% deposit on PO, balance net 30 after ship. Warranty + onsite options available as add-ons.
- Price: see attached quote — includes standard channel discounts but excludes shipping/tax.

Notes: Given current supply dynamics, H100 allocations are tight but predictable with an accepted PO and deposit. If ACME needs a tighter go-live, we recommend a hybrid approach: reserve cloud capacity for immediate activation and use OEM pod shipments to achieve steady-state.

I'll follow up with a formal quote document and local sales contact if you'd like to progress to PO.

Best,
Priya Singh
OEM Sales, NVIDIA OEM
Attachment: NVIDIA_QUOTE_20260216.pdf

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity timeline, OEM lead times & cloud reserve for ACME deal — procurement next steps

Team —

Summary and suggested procurement path for ACME (actionable):

1) Short-term (May go-live window): commit to a hybrid approach. Reserve 25% of capacity with AvaCloud (fast reservation, ~3–4 weeks to provision after deposit) + Redwood-managed routing to ensure predictable latency. This covers immediate launch traffic.
2) Medium-term (steady-state): place OEM PO for 60 H100-class nodes with NVIDIA per the quote. Expect 10–14 week lead time; request staged shipments to accelerate partial capacity.
3) Pricing: Marissa please prepare a 3-line comparison (monthly OPEX for full cloud reserve vs. hybrid vs. full OEM pod) factoring in the deposit amortization. Karthik, add uplift for premium SLA and managed on-call.
4) Procurement packet: Rafael will attach NVIDIA quote, AvaCloud reservation docs (Jake to confirm), the sizing note (Vivek), and the HubSpot deal link. We will ask ACME procurement to sign a short reservation deposit to lock dates.

Marissa — can you update the mutual action plan and push the DocuSign envelope once Jake confirms reservation terms?

I'll schedule a 30-min sync with ACME + Jake + Priya next week to align on dates and PO timing.

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
